text:
Maria K: Morning — quick heads up for today's weekly GPU capacity review. I uploaded the forecast workbook and the cluster-level burn rates. Link: https://internal.redwood/forecasts/2125
Ajay B: Saw it, thanks. Topline: US-west shows ~18% WoW increase; spot usage is at 62% in us-west-1.
Taylor R: Is that 62% preemptible on latency-critical shards? we should cap preemptible on latency-critical clusters.
Maria K: Good catch — spreadsheet breakdown: us-west batch pools ~48% spot, eu-prod inference ~62% spot.
Zoe (oncall): eu-prod also had NIC saturation alerts in the last 24h, + elevated retransmits on node-23. Not comfortable increasing spot there.
capacity-bot: forecast upload complete. 7-day burn projection attached. Peak hourly GPU-hours = 9800 at hour 60.
Ajay B: Proposed runbook: move 20% of scheduled batch jobs to the night window, and reduce concurrency for /embed route by 25% in eu region.
Taylor R: Agreed. Also propose changing autoscaler config for eu-prod: raise scale-up threshold from 70% -> 80% CPU to avoid noisy scale-ups when spot churn hits.
Maria K: That reduces ops churn but can increase tail latency. Can we compensate with KV prefix caching? Redwood Optimize suggested enabling prefix caching for ~15% of traffic.
Zoe (oncall): I can enable cache for a subset. Note: one cache backend is on an aging NFS mount — risk of eviction storms if load jumps.
Ajay B: On preemptible risk: propose adding reserved capacity for us-west shard-2: +4 V100-equivalent units for next 30 days. Cost delta rough: +$43k/month.
Taylor R: Can we also apply mixed-precision quantization for the batch-embedding model to drop GPU-hours by ~12%? Research has a patch ready.
Maria K: Patch review needed — @Taylor R can you coordinate? We can schedule a canary on a dedicated pool by Friday.
Zoe (oncall): Also flag: network egress limit for eu-gpu-high is 12TB/day. Marketing's Tue event could bust that if traffic spikes.
Ajay B: If egress is a hard cap, route some offload to us-east via async queue (increases latency slightly but keeps SLOs).
Taylor R: Spot prices are spiking in ap-southeast; for that region pin critical replicas to reserved leases and keep ephemeral scaling for background workloads.
Maria K: Action items: 1) Zoe to enable selective prefix cache and validate NFS risk (ETA 3h). 2) Ajay to submit reserved capacity request for us-west shard-2 (ETA EOD). 3) Taylor to run quantization canary on dedicated pool (ETA Fri). 4) Ops to throttle batch concurrency in eu (ETA 2h). 5) Finance to estimate cost delta (~+43k/mo) and alternatives.
Zoe (oncall): Starting cache toggle now, will post issues if any.
capacity-bot: alert: preemptible churn threshold breached in eu-prod (churn=0.18 > 0.15) — recommended fallback -> reserved.
Ajay B: Thanks bot. Quick check: any hot nodes showing thermal throttling? node-monitor reports: node-23 temp=92C across last 3 samples.
Taylor R: node-23 is also the NIC problem node — sounds like hardware replacement needed. Ops ticket created: https://tickets.internal/OPS-4091
Maria K: For the weekly readout slide, can someone pull the per-cluster burn table and a one-line risk summary for each region? I can assemble the deck.
Taylor R: I'll drop the table in drive in 30m. Include projected peak hour and % preemptible.
Zoe (oncall): If we reduce preemptible in eu by 20%, projected cost +$9k/mo but churn risk drops to ~0.08.
Ajay B: Acceptable given the enterprise deal on the pipeline.
Maria K: Also: Dedicated pool scaling policy bug — burst-capacity fallback isn't honoring model routing, causing retries. Ticket INF-572 logged with eng-runtime.
Taylor R: INF-572 is in triage, I'll ping Chris to expedite.
Zoe (oncall): Cache toggle complete, no immediate evictions. NFS latency elevated but within thresholds; monitoring for 4h.
Maria K: Closing notes: we'll do a midweek checkpoint if any action changes burn projections. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Ajay B: Thanks!
Taylor R: Thanks
capacity-bot: thread archived.
